sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Sneek, the main town of the municipality of Súdwest-Fryslân in Friesland, makes parking cheap for short visits and keeps through traffic out of the centre. Under the 2026 ordinance, adopted on 18 December 2025, street and surface parking costs 1.03 euros per half hour up to two hours and 1.54 euros beyond, and the first half hour of the day is free only if the licence plate is registered, whereas in 2025 it was free without conditions [0][2]. Paid hours are Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 21:00 and Sunday from 13:00 to 21:00, under a 2025 designation that lists about 32 paid streets and lots and that we did not find replaced [3][4]. A resident permit inside the canals costs 106.00 euros a year, a business permit 495.00 euros and a long-stay permit outside the canals 30.00 euros a month, the same as in 2025 [5]. A 2021 permit rule allows at most two permits per address, and a garage pass for holders of a subscription permit [6]. The municipality ran a trial of a low-traffic centre from 2 January 2024, with signs and cameras on through routes. Traffic on Prins Hendrikkade and Singel fell by 37 to 49 percent, against a target of 25, and the executive shortened the daily ban to 12:00-17:00 in March 2024 and withdrew the ban on Prins Hendrikkade in October 2024 after public incomprehension [8][9]. The Mobility Programme of 10 February 2026 aims to route through traffic around the centres of Sneek and Bolsward, with the car as a guest in the centre [11].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The direction is to take surface parking out of the centre. An amended environmental vision decided on 29 January 2026 says surface parking inside the centre zone is no longer wanted and is to be phased out, with parking explored in multifunctional built hubs at the edge, and it proposes to study built alternatives to surface parking in the Veemarkt and station zone; this is a long-term vision and not a construction programme [16][17]. The Mobility Programme lists as explorations a multifunctional station hub with a water-transport stop, upgraded transfer points and a search area on Oppenhuizerweg, none of them decided projects [12][13]. It says the municipality has a charging policy and lists expanding the charging network, without charger numbers for the town's car parks [14]. A 2022 traffic decision designated charging-only bays at five locations, two in Sneek among them [10]. For the Sneekweek of 31 July to 6 August 2026 the centre was closed to motor traffic from 19:00 to 02:30, and an attached map marks the parking sites around the town, without saying who operates them [15].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The two garages, P-Zuid Waterpoort and P-Oost Normandiaplein, are free for the first 24 hours and then cost 1.54 euros per half hour with a maximum of 5.00 euros a day, paid round the clock [1][3]. Q-Park lists the P+R at the station in Kanaalstraat as its only facility in Sneek, with 126 spaces, a 1.90 m height limit and round-the-clock access, and with a discount for rail travellers; its tariff did not load [18]. The garages and the park-and-ride are among the town's transfer points, which the programme says lie within a short walk of the inner city [12].

Our data cover the P+R in Sneek, with 126 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 52% on weekdays and 53% at weekends, so it is used about as much on Sundays as on workdays, and it reached full in a single reading on a Sunday morning. The garages and street parking are not in our data.
